text:
anna: Heads-up — saw a spike in onboarding latency this morning when the bench runs started running inline with the smoke checks. We should discuss splitting the paths so fast acceptance checks don't queue behind heavy perf benches.

devin: +1. Current pipeline serializes: ingest -> lightweight-smoke -> full-bench -> kv-compat. If full-bench is heavy the smoke waits and user-visible latency increases.

marta: We also need to be careful about false negatives for quantized variants. A quick pass that only checks top-1 tokens can miss decode-mode divergences.

kevin: How much extra infra if we decouple? Storage for artifacts, extra worker pools? rough numbers plz.

anna: Proposal sketch: two parallel lanes after ingest — "fast-accept" (0-10s, run on CPU or tiny GPU, checks signatures, basic decode sanity, smoke prompts) and "deep-bench" (async, longer, records perf, golden diffs). Fast-accept returns admission token. Deep-bench writes bench-report + compatibility flags.

sam: Love it. For fast-accept we should require a minimal manifest that includes model-arch, kv-schema, and a small golden-prompts zip. Example manifest snippet:```
name: example-model
arch: llama2
kv_schema: v1
golden_prompts: s3://redwood-onboard/gold/1234.zip
accept_thresholds:
  perplexity_delta: 15
  decode_confidence: 0.8
```

devin: Suggest making the manifest machine-friendly: add a `fast_checks` list with runnable checks (e.g., smoke_decode, embedding_dim_check, kv_roundtrip). That way fast-accept is pluggable.

marta: For quantized binaries add `numeric_tolerance` per op and a `quantize-mode` tag. If tolerance missing, don't auto-accept.

kevin: Cost: two smaller fleets recommended. Fast-accept can be s-1 nodes (cheap), deep-bench on g4/rtx depending on model. Estimated delta: +8% infra for parallelism, plus S3 for golden artifacts (~$50/mo per active model if we keep latest 3).

anna: Operational notes: we should gate route creation on fast-accept only. Deep-bench can trigger policy changes: if bench fails, mark model as `quarantine` and notify intake owners.

build-bot: deploy queued: updated intake lambda to emit `accept_token` and `bench_job_id` — CI pipeline will run smoke-suite on PRs.

sam: Rollout plan: 1) infra + manifest schema change behind feature flag, 2) run a few low-risk models through parallel lanes, 3) monitor admission latency and false-positives for 2 weeks, 4) flip default.

devin: One more tradeoff: decoupling raises eventual consistency risk — product teams may expect routes live only after deep-bench passes. We should make that explicit in docs and provide an opt-in to block route creation until deep-bench success.

marta: Also add a cheap KV smoke: `kv_put/get` with a 2MB payload to catch serialization/shape issues early.

anna: Agreed on docs. I'll draft a short RFC + manifest schema PR. Link to a rough doc: https://internal.redwood/inbox/onboard-parallel-lanes (WIP).

kevin: OK, if Anna posts numbers for infra and retention I'll budget it. :+1:

sam: tagging @platform-team for FYI and ops runbook integration.

anna: Thanks all — I'll open the RFC and a small prototype job that runs the fast-accept suite in <48h.

devin: tl;dr: separate fast acceptance from heavy bench, manifest-driven checks, opt-in strict gating for deep-bench, golden artifacts + quantized tolerances.

marta: 👍

kevin: 👍
